newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand has no plan to free corn imports yet.
newsitem.headline: Thailand has no plan to free corn imports yet.

text.p: Thailand does not plan to fully liberalise corn imports just yet as lower foreign product prices would hurt local farmers, Commerce Minister Narongchai Akrasanee said on Monday.
"We want to do that. But at the moment, the prices of local product are mostly higher than imported product and this will affect corn farmers," he told reporters.
Narongchai said authorities were checking local corn stocks to determine whether zero-tariff corn imports were needed and would announce a decision soon.
The government had originally set February 20 as the date for zero-tariff imports but had to postpone it due to complaints from corn farmers that imports would pressure local prices.

"It is a balancing act that we have to do, really. The import liberalisation would help lower production costs (for feed grain) and, consequently, stabilise food prices. But we cannot allow that to affect local farmers either," he said.
The government this year liberalised imports of soybeans. It also removed import quotas on soymeal and cut import tariffs to 10 percent from 15 percent previously.

The Thai feedmill industry has forecast that it would need to import between 300,000-400,000 tonnes of corn this year, the equivalent of one months' consumption. The rest would come from domestic output projected at 4.39 million tonnes for the 1996/97 season (July-June).
